# Margin Notes

A small Rails JSON application for storing notes and exporting them. It uses
PostgreSQL, Jbuilder, Redis caching, inline jobs, and a streaming endpoint.

## Project references

- Read [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for shared test conventions.
- Read [docs/guides/controllers.md](docs/guides/controllers.md),
  [docs/guides/models.md](docs/guides/models.md), and
  [docs/guides/views.md](docs/guides/views.md) for the layer you are changing.
- Read [docs/guides/fixtures.md](docs/guides/fixtures.md) when changing test data.
- Find similar code in this application before introducing a new pattern.

## Development commands

Run these from the application root. Ruby is pinned in `.ruby-version`;
`mise.toml` enables that idiomatic version file. Orb setup puts mise's shims on
`PATH`. In another Bash shell, activate mise once as shown below.

```sh
mise trust mise.toml
mise install
eval "$(mise activate bash --shims)"
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails server
bin/rails console
bin/rails dbconsole
bin/rails routes
bin/rails test
bin/rails test test/controllers/notes_controller_test.rb
bin/rails test test/models/note_test.rb
```

- Start PostgreSQL and Redis before running Rails commands. Orb setup manages
  them through Amp's service supervisor; `.agents/services` starts them again.
- Development uses `margin_notes_development`; tests use `margin_notes_test`.
- `PGHOST` and `PGUSER` select PostgreSQL access; `REDIS_URL` selects the cache.
- Request and SQL logs go to stderr, including when running tests.
- This app deliberately retains `config.load_defaults 7.0`; changing the installed
  Rails version is not the same operation as changing framework defaults.
- Keep local development signing settings out of any production deployment.

## Task-specific guidance

Load the applicable repository skills when changing these layers:

- `writing-rails-controllers` for controllers and request tests.
- `writing-rails-models` for model behavior and model tests.
- `writing-rails-views` for Jbuilder representations and their request tests.

Load more than one when a change crosses layers.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content:
Research redis 4.8.1 → 5.4.1 (agent aac497ab696a76411) completed.

Upgrading the `redis` gem from 4.8.1 to 5.4.1 looks low-risk for this app. The installed Rails (7.0.8.7) already supports redis-rb 5, and the only place the app touches Redis is the Rails cache store setting. I did not change anything, and I did not install the new version or run the tests.

**How the app uses Redis**
- `/app/Gemfile` line 6 pins `gem "redis", "4.8.1"`. `/app/Gemfile.lock` resolves `redis (4.8.1)` next to `rails` and `activesupport` 7.0.8.7.
- `/app/config/application.rb` lines 17-19 set `config.cache_store = :redis_cache_store` with only `url:` (from `REDIS_URL`) and `namespace:`.
- No app code calls the Redis client directly. A search for "redis" found nothing in `app/`, `lib/` or the tests: no `Redis.new`, no `Redis.current`, no hiredis driver, no `redis_cache_store` options beyond the two above. The other hits are docs, setup scripts and a comment in `config/environments/development.rb`.

**Does Rails 7.0.8.7 work with redis 5?**
- Yes. Rails 7.0.4 (September 2022) made `RedisCacheStore` and the Action Cable Redis adapter work with redis-rb 5.0, as a backport to the 7.0 branch. 7.0.8.7 includes that change.
- Keeping `config.load_defaults 7.0` doesn't matter here. Which redis versions work depends on the installed Rails version, not on the framework defaults setting.

**What changes in redis 5.x (summary from memory, not checked against the redis-rb changelog)**
- redis-rb 5 is rebuilt on top of the `redis-client` gem, so Bundler will add `redis-client` to `Gemfile.lock`. 5.4.x needs a fairly recent `redis-client`.
- Removed in 5: `Redis.current`, the old `driver: :hiredis` option (replaced by the separate `hiredis-client` gem), and some loosely typed command arguments. The app uses none of these.
- Ruby 3.2.9 (from `.ruby-version`) is well within what 5.x supports.

**Remaining risks and checks**
- Cache error handling: Rails 7.0.x's handling of Redis errors in the cache store has had small fixes since then (for example a `supports_expire_nx?` bug with distributed Redis). These shouldn't affect this app's simple single-URL setup.
- To upgrade: change the Gemfile pin to `"5.4.1"`, run `bundle update redis`, check that `redis-client` was added to the lockfile, and run `bin/rails test` with Redis running. Exercising cache reads and writes on the export endpoint would be a useful extra check.

Sources (mostly mirrors and bot pull requests quoting the Rails changelog; the official rails/rails CHANGELOG is worth checking before relying on them):
- [Rails 7.0.4 release notes (newreleases.io)](https://newreleases.io/project/gems/rails/release/7.0.4)
- [rubygem-activesupport-7.0 revisions, changelog excerpt (openSUSE)](https://build-test-1.opensuse.org/package/revisions/devel:ARM:Factory:Contrib:ILP32/rubygem-activesupport-7.0)
- [Bump activesupport 7.0.3.1 to 7.0.4.1 PR, changelog quote](https://github.com/olivere/atom_feed/pull/6/{{ revealButtonHref }})
- [OBS request with activesupport changelog](https://build.openbuildservice.org/request/show/1010047)
- [Rails activesupport mirror with commit history (demo.gitea.com)](https://demo.gitea.com/TEST_CODEOWNERS/rails/src/commit/92dcc9a09fb9c23e5ee3d35687bc48ee2bc062b4/activesupport)
